relevance_note: The paper reports six families with germline TNFAIP3 mutations causing A20 haploinsufficiency and describes named patients ('Patients P4, P6 and P5, who is the sister of P4 and aunt of P6, had in common oral/genital ulcers and polyarthritis'), so patient-level rows are possible.
method_note: No script was used; I read the full text, Table 1 and the figure legends, and transcribed Table 1 by hand. In scope are the patients of the six families. Families 3, 4 and 5 get no rows: the paper names a family and a variant (Table 1) but describes no person in them (no label, sex, age, count or feature), and I did not invent one; Table 1 is per family, not per patient. Label-free people follow rules 2 and 6: 'unnamed person 1' = the affected mother of Family 1, 'daughter of unnamed person 1 1/2' = her two affected daughters, 'unnamed person 2' = the Turkish index patient whose variant p.Pro268Leufs*19 was found in 'her two affected daughters'. The three 'unaffected family members' of Family 2 are given rows as tested relatives (related to P5 because the sentence names them together); Family 1's 'maternal unaffected family members' are not enumerated and get no rows. 'an affected sister of P6 had similar symptoms but was not available for this study' is an affected relative and gets a row but no variant row, because no variant is tied to her. Contradictions in the paper: Family 1 ancestry 'Caucasian' (text) vs 'European Canadian' (Table 1); Family 2 'Italian ancestry' (text) vs 'European American' (Table 1); '5 heterozygous truncating mutations in TNFAIP3 in five families' (text) vs six families (abstract and Table 1). cohort_size_as_stated (13) is the sum of the three groups stated in Human subjects (7+4+2); the paper also screened 150 patients and 384 Turkish plus 384 Japanese Behcet's cases, who are out of scope. No total number of TNFAIP3-variant patients is stated, so n_patients_reported is null. Table 1's '0 / 122,972' cells are an allele-frequency fraction, not stacked per-patient values, and no table contains stacked (' / ') patient values. Phenotypes of the three Family 1 patients and of P4/P5/P6 come from statements naming that family or those patients (evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement' for Family 1); the paper never assigns features to individual Family 1 members. Variant class, zygosity, pathogenicity, ACMG and functional data: 'frameshift' only for the Family 6 variant, which the text names; pathogenicity and functional results are given only at cohort level ('The identified mutations were considered pathogenic', 'Expression of wild type A20 was reduced in patients’ PBMCs'), so they stay 'not reported'. Inheritance stays 'not reported' because no carrier parent is named for any person; Table 1's 'Dominant'/'De novo' is per family and Family 4 has no person row. 'normalized markers of systemic inflammation' in Patient 6 was read as evidence of elevated inflammatory markers. I gave no autoantibodies row to any individual: 'five patients in our study developed autoantibodies' names no one, and I did not infer it for Patient 6 from the separate statement that an overt autoimmune disease was diagnosed only in her. Every checklist row repeats the individual's label with the same span used in the individuals table.
